existingDispositions.rationale: Institutional impartiality can be experienced as procedural fairness, but current sources are governance indicators and perception regressions rather than an independently identified institution-to-person effect.
Differential enforcement can be noticed as unfair, but differential treatment may be judged justified under relevant standards; neither source isolates this objective source.

External oversight is a real institutional condition; its effect on institutional trust requires exposure/credibility and later trust measurement, absent from the cited perception-regression evidence.
Service capacity is not satisfaction with a service. OECD measures perceptions; WGI is a composite. Exact capacity→trust identification remains missing.
Information about corruption can alter trust, but real corruption prevalence, trust and legitimacy are distinct; cited sources do not establish the exact negative legitimacy claim.
Specific norm perceptions can precede intentions, but assigned norm discrepancy and adolescent behavior syntheses do not establish isolated descriptive-norm→commitment effects.
Perceived approval and intention are related, but broad subjective-norm manipulations can bundle descriptive/approval and personal attitudes.
Procedural-justice packages and organizational justice correlations support a research direction, not uniform causal effects of every fairness facet on rightfulness.
Rightfulness may support voluntary compliance intention but policing programs do not independently manipulate legitimacy and then identify its effect on intention.
Functional perceived support can buffer stress-related outcomes, while integration measures often show main effects; these are not identical causal routes into perceived stress appraisal.
Perceived rejection and low belonging share content; randomized ostracism changes both but does not independently randomize the perceived-exclusion mediator.
Perceived exclusion→HPA/sympathetic stress requires independent mediation and physiological measures. RDoC constructs/units supply no segment-specific causal estimate.
Individual willingness to accept vulnerability differs from group cooperation prevalence. Current sources concern collective action/diffusion rather than isolated exact trust.
Norm-feedback experiments can influence individual behavior, but perceived norms are not independently randomized and group prevalence requires explicit aggregation.
Trust in competence/integrity is distinct from rightful authority; OECD does not identify this mediator-to-legitimacy segment.
Controlled ostracism exposure supports a bounded increase in perceived exclusion; exact game-aligned ratings converge in young-adult experiments.
Actual prevalence may inform perceived norm only when sampled/communicated; displayed survey statistics are not the actual group changing.
Publicly expressed approval may inform perceived approval, but private beliefs and expression are not identical; audience and salience select whose views are seen.
Contact quality could affect trust in a contact, but cited dehumanization/violence and topology-diffusion sources do not establish that exact person-target effect.

SOC-096 is an external RDS: group-status difference within a common field. An independently perceived disparity could influence fairness, but cited RD/collective-action reviews do not identify that exact route.
